rationale: Two questions of different kinds must be answered together: whether outcomes among all starters are in the expected range (quantitative, routine data) and why some people cannot use video (qualitative, interviews). A convergent mixed-methods design collects both over the same period and integrates them in a joint display that places completion and outcome by subgroup next to interview themes. The retrieved evidence settles the effectiveness of the format (c1, c2) and points to unequal completion and uptake (c3, c4) that interviews must explain.
alternatives: Randomised comparison of video and in-person classes (refused: effectiveness is already shown and the programme cannot be withheld)
Quantitative service evaluation alone (refused: cannot explain drop-out)
Interview study alone (refused: cannot tell whether outcomes are adequate)
guidelines: GRAMMS (Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial would repeat what is known and require withholding video delivery; a sequential design would delay the qualitative findings the hospital needs in 2027.

decision.statement: Run a convergent mixed-methods evaluation from October 2026 to June 2027: KOOS-12 change at three months for every starter, completion by age and internet access, and interviews with 16 to 20 participants sampled to include people who stopped.
decision.question: How should the service evaluate the video exercise programme before the hospital decides its future?

criteria.text: Video delivery gives pain outcomes similar to in-person exercise in people who can use it, so the open question is local outcomes and access.
Completion or uptake differs by internet access or language, which interviews can explain.
The hospital has already decided the programme's future before results are available.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval of the protocol including interviews
gates.evidence: Approval REB-26-0875 dated 2026-09-19, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Protected physiotherapist time for interviews and analysis
gates.evidence: Service manager approval MSK-2026-31 for 3 hours per week, October 2026 to June 2027, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Offer device loans and a setup call without evaluation
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; both gates rest on investigator-supplied approvals.

summary: Convergent mixed-methods design; the decision rests on four ledger claims and both gates are met.
